question: How does BSP scale CET across the Northeast?
html:
BSP scales CET in three phases. First it makes Massachusetts and Connecticut one company around Horton. Then it buys founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT. Then it shifts the mix toward recurring service contracts, aiming for ~3x revenue in 36 months (est.) (CET growth plan).

The template

  • BSP took Smith + Howard from ~100 people in one office to ~800 people, 11 locations and nine add-ons in 3.7 years, with nearly 4x revenue, then sold to TPG (CET growth plan).
  • CET starts larger. After NuWave and Horton it has roughly 260-290 people, $65-100M of pro forma revenue and $6-11M of EBITDA. These are low-confidence estimates from filings, not disclosed figures (CET growth plan).

Three phases

  • Phase 1, MA and CT: Integrate Horton and point it at 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects. The biggest are in New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk. Named examples include the Fairfield pump stations (~$36.1M) and Danbury resiliency work (~$3.2M) (CET opportunity radar).
  • Phase 2, adjacent states: Use CET's existing six-state licensing to buy from a 48-company screen with a ~$15.1M median revenue. The aim is to move before Pfingsten's NEC Group or Ridgemont's Crete United (CET growth plan).
  • Phase 3, recurring revenue: Add SCADA, pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency work. Advisors price service-heavy contractors 3 or more turns above project-heavy ones (CET growth plan).

Roadmap (all est.)

MonthRevenueEBITDAHeadcountLocations
0$80M$8.0M2754
12$115M$12.1M3907
24$170M$19.5M56010
36$240M$30.0M78013

Source: CET growth plan. Every row is a labelled assumption, not guidance.

Gaps to close

  • Targets do not yet match Phase 2. Nine of the top 10 ranked targets are in Massachusetts, and one is in Connecticut (CET add-on targets).
  • McDonald Electrical is a partial bridge. It already runs ANJ Electric, a RI/CT union contractor, as a division.
  • Target revenues are ZoomInfo estimates, and some conflict with headcount.
  • Pipeline is thin in RI and NH. The opportunity radar tracks 27 CT items and 25 MA items, but only 16 in ME, 9 in VT, 5 in NH and 4 in RI (CET opportunity radar).
  • Permits are a weak signal. September 2026 housing permits are residential only (MA 1,515 units, RI 166). They do not show infrastructure demand (Census building permits).
  • Data centers are a thin upside here. ISO-NE says data-center growth has lagged in New England. PJM is the real upside case (CET growth plan).
  • Baseline is unverified. Audited CET financials would replace the estimated revenue and margins.

Next actions

  1. Bid Cambridge neighborhood EV charging (due Nov 10, 2026) and the MassWildlife Roger Reed Hatchery generators and ATS (due Nov 25, 2026). Confirm MassDOT prequalification first (CET opportunity radar).
  2. Book engineer-of-record meetings for the CT pump-station programs in Fairfield, South Windsor, West Haven and Danbury (CET opportunity radar).
  3. Rebuild the add-on list with more RI, NH, ME and VT candidates. Open diligence on McDonald Electrical's ANJ division as the RI/CT entry.
  4. Pull the MassDEP 2026 IUP tables by hand to itemize the 76 Massachusetts clean-water projects (~$1.02B) (CET opportunity radar).
